run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T02:28:51Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is consistent with low-rate HTTP 503 responses emitted by frontend-proxy itself: its 'ingress' spans are recorded with STATUS_CODE_ERROR (15.21 error spans/hour against 27,090 non-error in the hour ending 02:46:22), and its access log shows '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' - i.e. the connection to the upstream frontend service was terminated before a response started - followed by a successful retry in the same trace. These errors are sporadic (1.1-5.6 error spans per 5m window) and were already present in the earliest available samples (~02:05-02:11Z), before the 02:28:51Z alert onset, so the error signal did not begin at the alert time. The frontend service itself shows 0 error spans in the hour ending 02:46:22, its pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, latency p99 is flat (frontend 0.74-0.95 s, frontend-proxy ingress 1.18-1.68 s), and memory/CPU are stable (frontend CPU ~0.05 cores with a chronic ~30% CFS throttling ratio throughout). Chaos Mesh NetworkChaos experiments visible in the namespace during 02:11-02:39 applied only to the two fraud-detection pods and the kafka pod, not to frontend or frontend-proxy. The alert's stated value 0.0111 (1.11%) could not be reproduced from the available series (span-based ingress error ratio is ~0.0004-0.0017) because the alerting rule is not loaded in this Prometheus. What terminates the frontend's upstream connections, and hence a single root object, remains unverified, so the conclusion is partial and no root cause is named.

claims.text: frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR: increase over the hour ending 02:46:22 is 15.21 error spans versus 27,090.25 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans, while its 'router frontend egress' spans show 0 errors (0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR).

The frontend-proxy ingress error count is low and oscillating over the whole sampled period: increase over 5m per step is 1.11-5.56 error spans at 02:05:51-02:45:51Z, with nonzero values already at 02:05:51, i.e. before the 02:28:51Z alert start.

The span-based frontend-proxy ingress error ratio (rate of STATUS_CODE_ERROR / rate of all ingress spans) at 1-minute resolution from 02:11:00 to 02:46:00Z ranges from 0 to 0.00174 (mostly ~0.00036-0.0014), not 0.0111.

The frontend-proxy container log records 503 responses with the response detail 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for requests such as GET /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N (02:27:28Z, 02:27:39Z), GET /api/data/?contextKeys=binoculars (02:28:40Z), GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4 (02:30:08Z) and GET /api/data/?contextKeys=travel (02:38:45Z).

In the matching traces the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span is recorded with error=true, http.status_code 503, otel.status_code ERROR, and its child 'router frontend egress' span to the frontend cluster is recorded with error="true" and http.status_code="0"; the same traces contain a second ingress span with http.status_code 200 whose frontend spans (POST /api/cart, /api/products) also return 200, so the trace shows a failed attempt plus a successful retry.

The frontend service has 0 error spans in the hour ending 02:46:22 (increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR",service_name="frontend"} = 0), as do checkout, payment and accounting; in the same hour frontend-proxy has 15.21, fraud-detection 5.07, ad 3.05 and recommendation 3.04 error spans.
Pods frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq are Running and ready with restart counts 0 (started 2026-11-18T01:49:53Z and 01:49:55Z).
Deployments frontend (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend) and frontend-proxy (demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy) report 1 desired, 1 available and 1 ready replica.

The frontend and frontend-proxy ReplicaSets were created at 2026-11-18T01:49:53Z and 01:49:55Z respectively, roughly 39 minutes before the 02:28:51Z alert start, so no new ReplicaSet (rollout) appeared around the alert onset.

All NetworkChaos experiments visible in events between 02:11:14Z and 02:39:00Z are named otel-demo-fraud-detection-kafka-network-partition-* and their 'Applied'/'Recovered' messages name only otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, otel-demo/fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and otel-demo/kafka-ff7884766-29vm9.

All 75 PodNetworkChaos events in namespace otel-demo in the visible window name only three pods: fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b (25 events), fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst (25) and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9 (25); no PodNetworkChaos event names a frontend or frontend-proxy pod.

The frontend container's CFS throttling ratio stays at ~0.275-0.364 of periods across 02:03:51-02:45:51Z with no change at the alert onset, while its CPU usage is ~0.024-0.055 cores and its memory working set rises only from 122,757,120 to 128,544,768 bytes over the same period.
Latency stayed flat across the alert onset: frontend-proxy ingress p99 is 1,179-1,675 ms and frontend service p99 is 740-955 ms for the 5m steps from 02:15:00 to 02:45:00Z.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) currently has every fault-injection flag at defaultVariant "off" (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure).
All five cluster nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False; the frontend and frontend-proxy pods both run on node i-029c97e90b3730286.
Endpoints for the frontend Service resolve to pod IP 100.96.4.88:8080 and for frontend-proxy to 100.96.4.190:8080, so the frontend Service was not empty at query time.

The 503s are produced by connection termination on the upstream side of frontend-proxy - the frontend pod closing/resetting a connection before a response is written (egress span http.status_code 0, error detail connection_termination, immediate successful retry) - rather than an application-level error response from frontend, whose own spans carry no error status. The condition inside the frontend that causes the resets (for example a keep-alive/connection-lifecycle race) is not visible in the available evidence.

Because nonzero frontend-proxy ingress error spans exist throughout the sampled period (before and after 02:28:51Z), an alert rule on an error rate with a threshold of 'above 0' would keep firing on this steady low background; the exact evaluation window and denominator that produced the annotated 0.0111 value could not be verified.

The error spans of fraud-detection (5.07/hour), ad (3.05/hour) and recommendation (3.04/hour) are separate background/fault signals unrelated to the frontend-proxy 503s; fraud-detection's errors coincide with overlapping NetworkChaos experiments against fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-kqd2b, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst and kafka-ff7884766-29vm9, so a chaos-induced fault is a candidate only for fraud-detection.

Rejected: a Chaos Mesh network fault on the frontend pod as the cause of the frontend-proxy 503s. Every PodNetworkChaos event in otel-demo during the window names only the two fraud-detection pods and the kafka pod, and every visible NetworkChaos experiment applies only to those three pods - including the partition active at 02:38:50Z-02:38:45Z when a frontend-proxy 503 to /api/data?contextKeys=travel was logged.

Rejected: a deployment rollout or container restart of frontend/frontend-proxy at alert time. Both ReplicaSets were created at 01:49:53-55Z, and both pods report restart count 0 with start times 01:49:53Z and 01:49:55Z.

Rejected: application-level errors raised inside the frontend service producing the proxy 5xx. The frontend service has 0 error spans in the hour ending 02:46:22, and the frontend spans in the failing traces carry http.status_code 200.

The alert annotation's current value 0.0111 (1.11%) is not reproducible from the frontend-proxy span data: the measured ingress error ratio at 1-minute steps from 02:11:00 to 02:46:00Z never exceeds 0.00174, so the quantity the rule evaluates (metric, denominator, window) is not the span-based error ratio observed here.

Frontend-proxy ingress errors did not start at the alert time: 5m increase was already nonzero at the earliest returned step (02:05:51Z) and 1-minute ratio values were nonzero at 02:11-02:18Z and 02:21-02:28Z, i.e. before 02:28:51Z.

Changed during the window for another reason: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst had its container 'fraud-detection' created and started at 02:28:53Z and carries restart count 1, close to the alert start but in a different service.

Inspect the frontend server's HTTP keep-alive/connection-close behaviour and the Envoy upstream connection-pool settings of frontend-proxy, since the observed failure mode is 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' with an immediate successful retry; collecting frontend stdout/stderr (no log lines were readable here) would show whether the server closes reused connections.

Recover the RequestErrorRate rule definition (expression, denominator, evaluation window, 'above 0' threshold) from the Alertmanager/Prometheus that owns it and compare it with the span-based ratio of ~0.0004-0.0017 measured here, so that a steady low-rate background cannot keep the alert permanently firing.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not loaded in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and no rule groups at all (both queries returned status no_data), so the rule expression, denominator, evaluation window and threshold that produced 'current: 0.01111111111111111' are unknown and the annotated value could not be reproduced.

The frontend container produced no readable log lines for 2026-11-18T01:28:51Z-02:46:22Z (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data for both an unfiltered and an error-filtered query, and no previous container instance exists), so frontend-side application behaviour at the moment of the resets could not be observed.

traces_span_metrics series for frontend-proxy only exist from about 02:05:51Z (a 24h range query returned a single point at the window end), so there is no pre-02:05 baseline and it cannot be determined whether the 0.0004-0.0017 ingress error ratio is normal for this deployment.

Chaos Mesh events are retained only from 02:11:14Z in this cluster, and NetworkChaos/PodChaos/HTTPChaos specs could not be read (chaos-mesh custom resources are outside the readable kind list), so any fault applied to frontend/frontend-proxy before 02:11:14Z, or the exact fault type/parameters of the visible experiments, remain unknown.

Which side terminates the frontend-proxy->frontend connection is unverified: there is no frontend-side error signal, no restart, and no readable frontend log, so the mechanism (for example an HTTP keep-alive race versus a network/traffic-layer reset) could not be established.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no record of configuration or environment changes around 02:28:51Z could be checked.
Kubernetes object state (pods, deployments, replicasets, endpoints, nodes) was read at query time (after the incident window) and cannot prove what those objects looked like at 02:28:51Z.
The reason pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst restarted its container at 02:28:53Z was not determined (its own logs would be needed); it is not evidence about the frontend-proxy alert.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule from the alerting Prometheus (or Alertmanager config management) to learn its metric, denominator and evaluation window, then recompute it for 02:20-02:35Z.
Collect frontend container stdout/stderr from the node (kubectl logs --previous / node log files) for 02:27-02:39Z to see whether the Node/Next.js server logs closed or reset connections.

Compare the Envoy upstream HTTP connection-pool settings of frontend-proxy (idle timeout, max requests per connection) with the frontend server's keep-alive settings, and consider raising/aligning them if the resets are an idle-connection race.
Review the chaos-mesh Schedule objects for otel-demo to confirm whether any schedule ever selects frontend/frontend-proxy pods, including before 02:11:14Z when events are no longer retained.
If sustained low-rate 503s are unacceptable, add a non-zero tolerance (e.g. a rate threshold or longer evaluation window) to RequestErrorRate so that a single upstream reset per window does not page.
